title: Close Hero, galaxy and canvas-picking browser acceptance gaps

scope.subject: Prove Hero deep links, Chinese galaxy Search travel and actual WebGL canvas picking all converge on the existing shared destination model

research_summary: The cloud suite already proves Personal Signal, observed exoplanet, native Moon, black hole, Earth, landmark, Search/Places, deep link and Journey contracts, but does not independently exercise Hero, galaxy or an actual WebGL pick. No production subsystem is missing: navigation.ts already resolves hero:aurora-01 and Chinese galaxy aliases, while YeisGalaxyScene already records data-yeis-picked-target whenever its real Input.onClick picker selects a destination. Reuse the existing Playwright harness and native Locate behavior. A deep-sky landmark can first be LOCATEd so the native controller centers it; after data-universe-locate-complete confirms settlement, a real pointer click at the canvas center should be resolved by the existing landmark sprite picker and route through onNavigateDestination. This avoids exposing test-only projection coordinates or invoking internal navigation functions.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS remains the native camera/input universe used by the existing destination and picking adapters; no alternative picker or navigation path is needed.
Playwright locator and mouse actions use the real browser input path and auto-wait for actionability, making them appropriate for acceptance of the actual WebGL interaction surface.
Playwright retrying locator assertions and expect.poll can wait on runtime evidence such as locate/travel completion without replacing product timing with arbitrary sleeps.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the existing YEIS native universe/input/navigation backbone; this task closes acceptance gaps around already-implemented destination types.
Reuse the existing Playwright browser harness for real keyboard/pointer/deep-link interaction and asynchronous runtime assertions.
Reuse native locate/travel and the existing canvas picker; do not add a diagnostic navigation API just for tests.
No additional component is required. Tests interact with the real Navigator and WebGL canvas.

candidates.name: Existing YEIS Hero/galaxy/canvas entry paths
candidates.license: Pinned MIT YEIS plus project-owned glue
candidates.reason: All requested entry points already resolve into UniverseNavigationDestination; the missing work is browser proof rather than a new implementation authority.

candidates.name: Existing Playwright real-input acceptance
candidates.reason: Covers URL reloads, keyboard Search, native locate settlement, real pointer input, runtime datasets and traces in the same harness already used for the rest of the product.

candidates.name: New test-only picking/projection API
candidates.reason: Would bypass the actual Input.onClick and sprite picking path, weakening rather than strengthening canvas acceptance.

decision.rationale: Add no production navigation code. Prove Hero with a shareable destination deep link, galaxy with the Chinese 仙女座 Search alias and actual native travel, and Canvas by centering a real deep-sky landmark through Locate then clicking the rendered canvas center and asserting data-yeis-picked-target plus the same destination executor.
decision.fallback: If a landmark's projected center is occluded by a higher-priority pick target, use another curated deep-sky landmark with no overlapping marker; do not add test-only production picking hooks.
